chunks: And from him, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, and others, regarding the names of the wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), their lineages, and their descriptions.

Ayesha, and Hafsa, and Umm Habeeb bint Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Zaynab bint Jahsh, and Sawda bint Zam'a, and Maymuna bint al-Harith, and Safiyya bint Hayy ibn Akhtab, and Umm Salama bint Abu Umayya, and Juwayriya bint al-Harith.

And Ayesha was from Taym, and Hafsa was from Adi, and Umm Salama was from Banu Makhzum, and Sawda was from Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, and Zaynab bint Jahsh was from Banu Asad; and a number of them were from Banu Umayya, and Umm Habib bint Abu Sufyan was from Banu Umayya, and Maymuna bint al-Harith was from Banu Hilal, and Safiyya bint Hayy ibn Akhtab was from Banu Israel.

And he (peace be upon him and his family) passed away with nine wives, and besides these were those who had gifted themselves to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and Khadeeja bint Khuwaylid, the mother of his child, and Zaynab bint Abi al-Jawn who was deceived, and al-Kindiya.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not marry (another wife) upon Khadeeja.

key_terms.لَمْ يَتَزَوَّجْ عَلَى: Did not marry upon (while she was alive)

ai.seo_question: Who were the wives of the Prophet Muhammad and what were their tribal lineages according to Shia sources?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi meticulously details the genealogical and tribal backgrounds of the Prophet’s wives, emphasizing their social status and lineage, which was crucial for understanding the political and social dynamics of early Islam. It distinguishes between the nine wives present at his death and other unique marital relationships, such as Khadija, while a supplementary report from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the Prophet did not contract a new marriage during Khadija’s lifetime, a point of scholarly discussion regarding the chronology of his marriages. This context highlights the Prophet’s marriages not merely as personal unions but as strategic alliances that reinforced tribal cohesion and social integration.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer, and someone else, ‘With regards to the names of the wives of the Prophetsaww, and their lineages, and their description – Ayesha, and Hafsa, and Umm Habeeb Bint Abu Sufyan Bin Harb, and Zaynab Bint Jahsh, and Sawda Bint Zam’a, and Maymouna Bint Al-Haris, and Safiyya Bint Hayy Bin Akhtab, and Umm Salmaas Bint Amayya, and Juweyriya Bint Al-Haris. And Ayesha was from (Clan of) Taym, and Hafsa was from Adayy, and Umm Salmaas was from the Clan of Makhzoum, and Sawda was from the Clan of Asad Bin Abdul Uzza, and Zaynab Bint Jahsh was from the Clan of Asad; and a number were from the Clan of Umayya, and Umm Habeeb Bint Abu Sufyan was from the Clan of Umayya, and Maymouna Bint Al-Haris was from the Clan of Hilal, and Safiyya Bint Hayy Bin Akhtab was from the Clan of Israil. And hesaww passed away leaving nine wives, and besides these wives were ones who had gifted themselves to the Prophetsaww, and Khadeejaas Bint Khuwaylid, a mother of hissaww child, and Zaynab Bint Abu Al-Jawn who was deceived, and Al-Kindiyat’.[1454] (p.s. - This is not a Hadeeth) Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that Rasool-Allahsaww did not marry (an additional wife) upon Khadeejaas’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘ Asem ibn Hamid from abu Basir and others about the names of the wives of the Holy Prophet, and their relations and qualities has said the following: “

The names of the wives of the Holy Prophet, were: ‘A’ishah, Hafsah, ‘Umm Habib daughter of abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Zaynab daughter of Jahash, Sawdah daughter of Zam‘ah, Maymunah daughter of al- Harith, Safiyah daughter of Hay ibn Akhtab, ‘Umm Salamah daughter of abu ‘Umayyah and Juwayriyah daughter of al-Harith.

‘A’ishah was from the tribe of Tamim, Hafsah from the tribe of ‘Adiy, ‘Umm Salamah was from tribe of banu Makhzum. Sawdah was from tribe of banu Asad ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza’, Zaynab daughter of Jahash was from the tribe of banu Asad, certain ones were from banu ‘Umayyah, ‘Umm Habib daughter of abu Sufyan was from the tribe of banu ‘Umayyah, Maymunah daughter of al-Harith was from the tribe of banu Hilal and Safiyah daughter Hay Akhtab was from banu Israel.

He (the Messenger of Allah), O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, died and he had nine wives. Besides these there were those who had given themselves as a gift to the Holy Prophet. Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid was (his first wife and) the mother of his children. Also of his wives were Zaynab daughter of abu al-Jawn who was deceived and al-Kindiyah.”
